LESSON: ACTIVE LISTENING, INTERACTIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.9: Active Listening, Interactive speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Active Listening, Interactive speaking. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you do to show you are listening actively?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the language structures and vocabulary in given listening contexts
2. show appreciation for turn-taking in dialogues

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ACTIVE LISTENING, INTERACTIVE SPEAKING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Active Listening, Interactive speaking helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: ACTIVE LISTENING, INTERACTIVE SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Explain the language structures and vocabulary in given listening contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the language structures and vocabulary in given listening contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the language structures and vocabulary in given listening contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Active Listening, Interactive speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the language structures and vocabulary in given listening contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Show appreciation for turn-taking in dialogues

What this means
In this part you learn to show appreciation for turn-taking in dialogues. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show appreciation for turn-taking in dialogues.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Active Listening, Interactive speaking to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show appreciation for turn-taking in dialogues. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Active Listening, Interactive speaking is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Active Listening, Interactive speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain the language structures and vocabulary in given listening contexts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Active Listening, Interactive speaking to a partner. (skill: show appreciation for turn-taking in dialogues)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Active Listening, Interactive speaking to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the language structures and vocabulary in given listening contexts.
3. Practise this skill: show appreciation for turn-taking in dialogues.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Active Listening, Interactive speaking from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Active Listening, Interactive speaking: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Active Listening, Interactive speaking?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you do to show you are listening actively?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Active Listening, Interactive speaking means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the language structures and vocabulary in given listening contexts.
5. Be able to: show appreciation for turn-taking in dialogues.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
